title: OPEC+ Announces Surprise Production Cut
content: OPEC+ ministers agreed on Sunday to an unexpected cut of 1.5 million barrels per day to crude output beginning next month, citing the need to stabilize a market they described as oversupplied. Brent crude jumped more than 4 percent in early trading as the cartel signaled it would defend higher price levels. Analysts said the tighter supply backdrop could keep energy costs elevated through the summer, raising input prices for airlines, shippers and chemical producers while boosting cash flows for major oil companies.

title: Shipping Slows Through the Strait of Hormuz Amid Naval Incidents
content: Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz slowed sharply this week after a series of naval incidents raised fears of disruption to the world's most important oil chokepoint. Several tankers diverted or anchored offshore, and war-risk insurance premiums for the route climbed to multi-year highs. Roughly a fifth of global crude passes through the strait, and traders warned that any sustained closure would send oil prices spiking and ripple through global supply chains.

title: US Tightens Sanctions on Iranian Oil Exports
content: Washington unveiled a fresh package of sanctions targeting Iranian oil exports and the shadow fleet of tankers used to evade existing restrictions. The measures aim to choke off a key source of revenue for Tehran and could remove hundreds of thousands of barrels per day from global markets. Energy strategists said the move adds a geopolitical risk premium to crude prices at a time when spare capacity is already thin.

title: Fed Officials Signal More Rate Hikes May Be Needed
content: Federal Reserve officials signaled they are prepared to raise interest rates further if inflation fails to cool, according to remarks from several policymakers this week. The hawkish tone surprised investors who had expected the central bank to pause. Treasury yields rose and equity futures slipped as markets repriced the path of monetary policy. Higher rates increase borrowing costs and tend to weigh on stock valuations, particularly for richly valued technology shares.

title: US Inflation Runs Hotter Than Expected
content: US consumer prices rose more than expected last month, with the core index accelerating on stubborn services inflation. The hotter reading dampened hopes for near-term rate cuts and pushed the dollar higher against major currencies. Economists said the data complicates the Federal Reserve's task and keeps the risk of additional tightening on the table, a backdrop that historically pressures both bonds and equities.

title: Weak Jobs Data Revives US Recession Fears
content: A sharp slowdown in hiring and a jump in jobless claims revived fears that the US economy is sliding toward recession. Manufacturing surveys also pointed to contracting activity, and investors rotated out of cyclical stocks into defensive assets. The combination of slowing growth and sticky inflation has stoked concerns about stagflation, leaving risk appetite fragile across global markets.

title: Apple Posts Record Quarter on Strong iPhone and Services Growth
content: Apple reported record quarterly revenue late Friday, beating Wall Street estimates on the back of strong iPhone demand and double-digit growth in its high-margin services business. The company also raised its dividend and expanded its buyback program. Shares rose in after-hours trading as management struck an upbeat tone on the product pipeline, although it flagged ongoing component cost pressures tied to global supply disruptions.

title: Alphabet Unveils Advanced Multimodal AI Model
content: Alphabet unveiled its most advanced multimodal artificial intelligence model to date, deeply integrating it across Search, Workspace and its cloud platform. Executives said the technology would open new advertising and enterprise revenue streams and cement the company's leadership in generative AI. Investors welcomed the announcement, betting that improved monetization could offset rising data-center spending.

title: Bitcoin Rallies on Spot ETF Approval Speculation
content: Speculation intensified that US regulators are close to approving several spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds, triggering a broad rally across digital assets. Bitcoin climbed toward recent highs as traders bet that ETF access would unlock fresh institutional demand. Market participants cautioned that volatility could spike around any official decision, and that a delay would quickly reverse the gains.

title: Global Supply Chain Disruptions Worsen as Ports Congest
content: Renewed port congestion and a wave of factory shutdowns are snarling global supply chains, lengthening delivery times and lifting freight rates. Manufacturers warned of higher input costs and possible production delays heading into the second half of the year. The disruptions threaten corporate margins across autos, electronics and consumer goods, and could add to inflationary pressure just as central banks weigh their next moves.

title: Saudi Arabia Extends Voluntary Oil Output Cuts Into Next Quarter
content: Saudi Arabia said it would extend its voluntary cut of one million barrels per day through the end of the next quarter, reinforcing OPEC+ efforts to tighten global crude supply. The kingdom signaled it was prepared to do whatever it takes to support prices, and traders read the move as a firm floor under the market. The extension comes on top of the cartel's broader production curbs and is expected to keep upward pressure on energy prices and on the fuel costs faced by transport and industry.

title: Libya Halts Output at Major Oil Field After Unrest
content: Libya halted production at one of its largest oil fields after renewed unrest disrupted operations, removing several hundred thousand barrels per day from global supply. The outage adds to a string of disruptions tightening the crude market and pushed benchmark prices higher. Analysts warned that the loss of Libyan barrels, combined with cuts elsewhere, leaves little spare capacity to absorb further shocks and keeps the risk premium on oil elevated.

title: Russian Refinery Outage Tightens Global Diesel Supply
content: A major Russian refinery went offline following a fire, squeezing already tight global diesel and refined-product markets. Crack spreads widened sharply as traders scrambled to secure alternative supply. The disruption threatens to lift fuel costs for transport and industry worldwide and adds another layer of risk to an energy market already strained by upstream production cuts.

title: Dollar Surges to Multi-Month High as Rate-Cut Bets Fade
content: The US dollar surged to a multi-month high against a basket of currencies as investors abandoned bets on near-term interest-rate cuts. Hawkish central-bank commentary and firm inflation data drove yields higher and burnished the greenback's appeal. A stronger dollar weighs on the euro and other major currencies and tightens financial conditions for emerging markets and commodity importers.

title: Treasury Yields Spike as Bond Selloff Deepens
content: US Treasury yields spiked to fresh highs as a deepening bond selloff reflected fears that interest rates will stay elevated for longer. The move rippled across asset classes, pressuring equity valuations and lifting borrowing costs for companies and households. Strategists said the repricing of rate expectations was punishing the most rate-sensitive corners of the market, including high-growth technology shares and the broad equity benchmarks.

title: Tech Stocks Slump as Investors Flee High Valuations
content: Technology stocks slumped as investors rotated away from richly valued shares amid rising interest rates and a more cautious risk appetite. The selloff hit megacap names hardest, dragging broad equity indexes lower. Market participants said stretched valuations left little cushion against the higher-rate backdrop, and warned that further volatility was likely if monetary policy stayed restrictive.

title: Apple Hit With Sweeping Antitrust Lawsuit Over App Store
content: Apple was hit with a sweeping antitrust lawsuit accusing the company of abusing its dominance over the App Store and stifling competition. Regulators are seeking sizable penalties and structural remedies that could force changes to a highly profitable services business. The legal overhang adds uncertainty for investors and could pressure the company's shares despite its recent strong results.

title: Adidas Raises Full-Year Guidance on Strong Footwear Demand
content: Adidas raised its full-year guidance, citing robust demand for new footwear lines and improving margins after a period of heavy discounting. Management struck an optimistic tone about the second half, pointing to strong order books across key regions. The upbeat outlook lifted sentiment toward the sportswear sector, though some analysts cautioned that rising input costs and a cooling consumer could temper the gains.

title: Markets Mixed as Traders Weigh Growth and Inflation Risks
content: Global markets were mixed as traders weighed signs of slowing growth against persistent inflation, leaving major indexes little changed on the day. Gains in energy and defensive sectors offset weakness in technology, while currency and bond markets traded in narrow ranges. Investors said the lack of a clear catalyst kept positioning cautious ahead of upcoming economic data.

title: Bitcoin Wavers as Risk-Off Mood Grips Markets
content: Bitcoin wavered and gave back some recent gains as a risk-off mood swept across markets, with investors trimming exposure to speculative assets. The pullback came despite continued optimism about potential exchange-traded fund approvals, highlighting the tug-of-war between structural demand and macro headwinds. Traders said digital assets remained highly sensitive to shifts in broader risk sentiment.
